incidente.resumo: Sun Enterprise servers shipped with cache modules containing faulty S-RAM chips and no ECC protection; stray radiation flipped bits, and on detecting a memory error the servers shut down and rebooted, causing repeated crashes at customer sites over more than a year. At the time of the article Sun was replacing cache modules on servers that had crashed and was starting to ship mirrored cache modules; some customers installed software that finds and corrects memory errors.

descricao.texto: High-end Sun servers at customer sites suddenly crashed for no apparent reason; customers sought repairs and complained to Sun.
trechos: At a new Web company in San Francisco, a telecommunications company in the Midwest, a Baby Bell in Atlanta, anInternet domain registry on the East Coast--for no apparent reason, high-end servers made by Sun Microsystems suddenly crashed.
For months Sun told customers seeking a repair that they must sign a legal agreement promising to keep it secret.
Verisign complained but got no explanation.

gatilho.texto: Stray radiation, alpha particles or cosmic rays disrupted memory, turning a 1 into a 0 or vice versa.
trechos: The faulty chips are easily disrupted by stray radiation, alpha particles or cosmic rays. The trouble occurs at the bit level--a 1 turns into a 0, or vice versa.When the computer detects an error in memory, it shuts down and reboots itself.

descricao.texto: Sun had been shipping servers whose cache modules contained faulty S-RAM chips from an unnamed supplier that are easily disrupted by radiation; the servers lack ECC protection, and when the computer detects a memory error it shuts down and reboots.
trechos: In May, after months of struggling to identify the cause, Sun discovered it had been shipping servers whose cache modules contained faulty S-RAM (static random access memory) chips from a supplierit won't name.

The faulty chips are easily disrupted by stray radiation, alpha particles or cosmic rays. The trouble occurs at the bit level--a 1 turns into a 0, or vice versa.When the computer detects an error in memory, it shuts down and reboots itself.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: High altitude, high temperatures and other factors can contribute to the problem.
trechos: High altitude, high temperatures and other factors can contribute to the problem.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The problem did not reproduce in long-running tests but reappeared once the machine was back in its environment, and it took months to identify the cause.
trechos: "You can run tests for a long time, and the problem doesn't happen. Then you put the machine back into its environment and you get the problem. It took us months just to figure out what was going on," says Shoemaker.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: When the crashes began, Sun believed the problem was caused by a flaw in customer data centers rather than in its servers.
trechos: When the crashes began over a year ago, Sun believed the problem was caused not by its boxes but by some flaw in customer data centers.

passos.texto: Sun replaced cache modules on servers that crashed at least at BellSouth Technology Service, and makes repairs case by case for customers who have had a problem.
trechos: At BellSouth Technology Service Sun has already replaced modules on servers that crashed, says Richard Liddell, a BellSouth vice president.
"We're dealing with this on a one-to-one basis with customers who have had a problem," says John Shoemaker, the executive vice president in charge of Sun's high-end server business.

passos.texto: Some customers fixed the problem by installing special software that can find and correct memory errors.
trechos: In the meantime some customers have fixed the problem by installing special software that can find and correct memory errors.

acoes.texto: In progress: Sun is delivering a new mirrored cache (two modules, one backing up the other) to replace defective modules only where needed; the new modules begin shipping this month and Sun will install them free for customers whose machines have crashed.
trechos: For now Sun is racing to deliver a new "mirrored" cache to replace defective modules in the field, although only where needed.
The mirrored cache has two modules. If one fails, the other backs it up. The new modules begin shipping this month. Sun will install them, free, for customers whose machines have crashed.

acoes.texto: Planned: Sun's next high-end servers, based on the UltraSparc III processor and due in mid-2001, will have ECC protection.
trechos: Its next high-end servers, based on a new processor called the UltraSparc III, will have ECC protection; they are to debut in mid-2001.

observacoes: A long-standing intermittent hardware problem without a bounded outage, so duracao is null; one customer, Verisign Global Registry Services, was down for two hours after a crash. The article gives no year for the incident (only relative times such as "late last year" and "Last November"). status_relatorio is preliminar because the article was written while repairs were still ongoing ("We're a few months away from working our way out of this thing"). The article also covers Sun's handling of customers (nondisclosure agreements, no public warning), which is not included as a factor.
